# Results — Study 808 (Continuing Overreaction)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Byun,
Lim & Yun (2016): a **weighted signed-momentum** score (weight the *signs* of the more
recent monthly returns more heavily) predicts the cross-section **positively**, so a
long-high-CO / short-low-CO book should earn a positive spread. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Stamped
as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **continuing-overreaction** score: the normalised recency-weighted sum of the **signs** of its trailing **12 monthly returns**, **skipping the most recent month** (`w_p ∝ p+1`, oldest→newest — recent months count most; the Byun-Lim-Yun `w_j = (n−j)` shape), known through month `i−2` |
| Sort | each month rank the cross-section by the CO score; **long the top 30%** (high CO), **short the bottom 30%** (low CO), equal-weight; measure the month-`i` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through month `i−2`, the most-recent month `i−1` skipped, hold month `i`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per monthly rebalance; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the monthly spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Momentum
and its cousins are documented largely on the broad cross-section including smaller names; a
50-mega-cap survivor panel is a thin, well-arbitraged slice where a signed-momentum tilt is
least likely to bite — which is what we find.

## The headline — long-high-CO / short-low-CO spread

Monthly equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% CO spread (n = **184** months):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-CO − short low-CO)** | **+15.46 bps/month** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **+0.58** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.55 |
| high-CO book / low-CO book | +152.94 bps / +137.48 bps (Welch *t* = +0.31) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost, ann.) | 0.14 |

The spread has the **right sign** — the claimed continuation direction (high-CO names earn a
touch more than low-CO names) — but it is **statistically indistinguishable from zero**: NW
*t* = +0.58, a monthly Sharpe of 0.14. The high-CO and low-CO books earn essentially the same
(+152.9 vs +137.5 bps/month, Welch *t* = +0.31). On this liquid mega-cap universe the famous
weighted-signed-momentum edge is **absent**, not reversed — just noise.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread more than luck?

Keep the CO sort but read each month's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+15.46 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +1.33 bps (20.82) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+0.68σ** (right-tail p = **0.261**) |

The observed spread sits barely two-thirds of a standard deviation above a null centred at
zero — right in the fat middle of the permutation distribution. There is no evidence the sort
found anything a random relabelling of names would not.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=82) | +8.23 bps | +0.26 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=102) | +21.27 bps | +0.54 |

Both halves are the same story: a small positive point estimate, no significance. Nothing to
see in either era.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per monthly rebalance; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/mo | cost/reb | net/mo | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +15.46 bps | 6.17 bps | **+9.29 bps** | +0.33 | 0.08 | +1.1%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +15.46 bps | 14.17 bps | **+1.29 bps** | +0.05 | 0.01 | +0.2%/yr |

Even before costs the edge is insignificant; the monthly round-trip friction then eats most of
the +15 bps point estimate, leaving a net *t* of +0.33 (1 bp) collapsing to +0.05 (5 bps). No
version of the book is a paycheck. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent monthly **trend state** that drives both
the recent monthly signs (so a weighted signed momentum proxies it) and — with `edge>0` — the
forward month. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.47** (sd 0.95), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.02`, seed 808) | **+8.61** (Welch *t* = +5.86) |

The detector recovers a *planted* continuation cleanly and stays silent on the null — so the
flat real-tape result is a true null on the mega-cap universe, not a broken sort.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Byun-Lim-Yun weighted-signed-momentum ("continuing overreaction")
  premium does **not** replicate on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-high-CO /
  short-low-CO spread is **+15.46 bps/month** with NW *t* = **+0.58** — the right *sign* but
  statistically zero, ≈+0.68σ in a 1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.261), and flat in both
  eras (*t* = +0.26 / +0.54). The 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* continuation
  cleanly (*t* = +8.61, fires on 1/20 nulls), so this is a genuine null, not a machinery
  failure. Survivorship biases the magnitude upward if anything.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The book is insignificant gross (+15.46 bps/month, *t* = +0.58) and
  the monthly round-trip friction eats it to +9.29 bps/month (net *t* = +0.33) at 1 bp, +1.29
  bps (*t* = +0.05) at 5 bps. No costed version pays.
